name: Speaksee Microphone Kit
oneLine: A clip-on microphone kit with a phone app that captions in-person group conversations, one colour per speaker, for deaf and hard of hearing people.

platforms.detail: The Speaksee app runs on iOS and Android and connects to the kit. Others can follow a session on a phone, tablet or computer through a shared link or QR code.

deviceRequirements.detail: The app works only with the Speaksee Microphone Kit, on a phone or tablet with Bluetooth Low Energy; the App Store lists iOS 16.6 or later. A minimum Android version is not stated, and the kit can't connect directly to a laptop.

roomCaptions.detail: Speech is picked up by the kit's microphones, which the speakers wear. The app is not a standalone app and doesn't caption with the phone's own microphone.

groupConversations.detail: The kit comes with 3 wearable microphones and a base station, and a second kit can be added. Speaksee's website says groups of up to 9; its store listings say up to six speakers at the same time.

languages.detail: Speaksee's help centre lists 11 languages tested by native speakers (such as Dutch, English, French, German and Spanish) and 44 more not yet tested, many of them regional variants.

offline.detail: The manual lists an internet connection as a requirement (Wi-Fi, or the phone's connection over Bluetooth), because audio goes to the Speaksee cloud. The kit uses about 40 MB of data an hour.

speakerLabels.text: Yes, a colour and name per mic
speakerLabels.detail: Each microphone's speech shows in its own colour, and each microphone can be given a name and a language in the app.

translation.text: Yes, live, a language per mic
translation.detail: You can set the spoken and shown language for the whole session or for each microphone, and people following by QR code can read in their own language. The August 2026 manual says 80+ languages; the product page says more than 40.

saveTranscripts.text: Yes, as a file on your device
saveTranscripts.detail: After a conversation you can save the transcript to the phone (Files on iPhone and iPad, Downloads on Android). Speaksee deletes transcripts from its own servers shortly after use, so the saved file is your copy.

export.text: File on device; live link or QR
export.detail: Transcripts are saved as a file on the device; the file format is not stated. A live session can be shared with others through a link or QR code.

fileUpload.detail: Transcribing uploaded audio or video files is not mentioned on Speaksee's pages.

summaries.detail: AI summaries are not mentioned on Speaksee's pages.

customWords.text: Word list sent through a web form
customWords.detail: You can add names, technical terms and abbreviations by sending a word list through a form on the help centre; it is not described as a setting in the app.

display.detail: The app offers four themes (Color, Glow, Minimal, Teletext), dark mode, focus mode, text size and bold words.

soundAlerts.detail: Alerts for sounds other than speech are not mentioned.

phoneCalls.detail: Speaksee's help centre says the Microphone Kit is not designed for phone calls; it captions conversations around you.

videoCalls.detail: The kit is for in-person conversations. Speaksee sells separate AutoCaption software that captions a Windows computer's sound, such as online meetings; it runs on Windows only and is priced by quote.

mediaOnDevice.detail: AutoCaption captions audio playing on a Windows computer. The kit's base station has a 3.5 mm input for a phone or TV, but Speaksee says this is not fully supported yet.

humanCaptioners.detail: No human captioners are offered; captions are automatic.

privacy.text: Cloud in the EEA; not used for training
privacy.detail: Audio is processed in the cloud by Speaksee and third-party speech-to-text processors within the European Economic Area, encrypted, and is never used for training. The privacy policy says transcripts are deleted within 5 minutes; the help centre says right after processing.

account.text: Yes, plus a kit activation code
account.detail: You create a Speaksee account (Google, Apple or email) and enter the activation code from the kit box; each code works for one account.

availability.detail: Speaksee doesn't publish a country list. Its help centre covers funding in the UK and the Netherlands, the kit is safety-tested for the EU, UK, US, Canada and Australia, and a Canadian reseller sells it.

freePlan.text: No; the app needs the paid kit
freePlan.detail: The app is free to download but works only with the Speaksee Microphone Kit, which comes with a paid software subscription. Speaksee says a trial is possible in some cases.

price.detail: Speaksee publishes no prices and asks you to request a quote. Canadian reseller Special Needs Computers lists the 3-microphone kit at CA$2,029.99, the 6-microphone kit at CA$2,999.99 and a one-year Speaksee subscription at CA$2,800.00 (October 2026).

accessibilityFunding.detail: In the UK, Speaksee points employees to Access to Work and students to the Disabled Students' Allowance. In the Netherlands, contracted health insurers usually pay the full cost (your deductible applies), and work use can be paid through the UWV.

strengths.text: Each speaker wears their own microphone, so captions are split by speaker with a colour and name for each; Speaksee says it works in groups and with background noise.
A session can be shared live by link or QR code to other phones, tablets or computers, and each microphone can be translated into another language.
Funding routes are documented for the UK (Access to Work, DSA) and the Netherlands (health insurance, UWV), where the kit can be fully funded.
Audio is processed in the EEA under GDPR and is not used for training, and Speaksee states ISO 27001 certification.

limits.text: The app works only with the Speaksee Microphone Kit; it can't caption with the phone's own microphone.
Prices are not published; a Canadian reseller lists CA$2,029.99 for the 3-mic kit plus CA$2,800.00 for a one-year subscription.
Captioning needs an internet connection because audio is sent to the Speaksee cloud.
The microphones must be worn (not placed on a table) and last about 4 hours per charge; phone calls are not supported.

notes: Speaksee publishes no prices on its own site or help centre (quote only). The CAD prices come from a third-party Canadian reseller, Special Needs Computers (s26, s27; kit prices re-checked in its product JSON: 2029.99 and 2999.99 CAD); the reseller lists the kit as a one-time purchase plus an annual subscription. EUR figures seen only in a search snippet of a European assistive-technology database record (not opened, behind a Cloudflare challenge) are not used. UK reseller pages blocked access. Conflicts: group size is 'up to 9 participants' on the website vs 'up to six speakers' in both store listings; translation is '40+ languages' on the product page vs '80+' in the August 2026 manual; transcripts are deleted 'immediately after processing' (help centre) vs 'within 5 minutes after usage' (privacy policy dated 12-01-2025). The manual lists 'Wi-Fi internet connection' as a requirement but also says Bluetooth mode uses the phone's internet. The language list (re-counted 2026-10-28) has 55 entries including regional variants and near-duplicates (Zulu and IsiZulu, Bahasa Melayu and Malaysian). On the App Store the app is an iPad app that can run on Apple silicon Macs, marked 'Not verified for macOS'. speak-see.com and the reseller rate-limited direct downloads, so s1, s2, s19, s26 and s27 were read through WebFetch; help-centre, manual and store quotes were checked against the raw page text. Speaksee also sells Soundshape 1 Pro, an event captioning product, not covered here.
